$comment: S6 cannot be disabled. It is the rule that refuses to pay in the wrong token, under a scheme we do not implement, or to a recipient that cannot receive. Under the x402 `exact` scheme, creating the recipient's token account is the ENDPOINT's responsibility — saying so in the message is what makes it actionable by whoever can fix it.

cases.name: pass · the network's USDC, the exact scheme, a recipient that can receive
fail · a scheme we do not implement
boundary · the right network, but the OTHER network's USDC mint
cases.$why: The key, the agent and the challenge all say sandbox, so S0 passes — and the mint is still wrong. This is why the mint is checked as well as the network.

cases.name: fail · the recipient has no token account for this mint
fail · a challenge asking for an unrelated token
